  "markdown_report": "**Proposed direction: calibrate diagnostic execution and fault detection before interpreting activation patches.** At 20% progress, bounded calibration is feasible without changing any category’s single NextItNet predictor. It does not establish circuit-localization accuracy.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Movies and CDs have positive old-minus-random contrasts: older substitutions disrupt less, without showing harmful older history. (2) Electronics’ 9.38% negative-over-positive training rate motivates investigation, not a validation conclusion. (3) Existing controls cover several contracts, but export parity remains unverified. Passing controls does not demonstrate fault-detection power.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [DeepCrime](https://huang.isis.vanderbilt.edu/cs8395/readings/testing-dl.pdf) distinguishes prediction changes from label-grounded degradation; its statistical killing protocol does not transfer to one frozen checkpoint. (2) [MuFF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09846) motivates separating mutation activation, behavioral effects, and detector alarms. Its sensitivity metric is not detector sensitivity. (3) [Zhang–Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) and [ACDC](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/34e1dbe95d34d7ebaf99b9bcaeb5b2be-Paper-Conference.pdf) motivate separate calibration of intervention effects and known-path recovery.

Three directions follow: implementation detection, intervention reliability, and evaluation scope. The framework becomes **specified fault → execution witness → independent contract outcome → frozen diagnostic alarm → limited interpretation**. Natural-model localization remains exploratory.

| Atomic idea | Originality / potential / difficulty | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A. Calibrate isolated diagnostic mutations [DeepCrime, MuFF] | 3 / 6 / 5 | Originality: useful NextItNet integration; established testing. Potential: exposes blind spots; limited fault coverage. Difficulty: bounded frozen executions; independent oracles require care. |
| B. Check hybrid-activation distances [Zhang–Nanda] | 4 / 6 / 5 | Originality: architecture-specific transfer; familiar checks. Potential: flags outliers; normal distances cannot certify validity. Difficulty: bounded caching; reference selection is delicate. |
| C. Compare permitted sampled/full-catalog ranks [Krichene–Rendle] | 3 / 6 / 5 | Originality: useful integration; established comparison. Potential: reveals candidate dependence; cannot replace pinned evaluation. Difficulty: simple scoring; catalog scans cost time. |
| D. Recover known synthetic paths [ACDC] | 4 / 7 / 7 | Originality: recommendation adaptation; established principle. Potential: tests localization; synthetic transfer is uncertain. Difficulty: exact references; additional infrastructure. |

**Select A**, with D as later localization calibration. Inject incorrect `count−1` readout, future-feature mixing, and constant history features separately through the actual diagnostic execution path. Use unchanged and identity-hook controls. Treat constant features as a behavioral challenge unless an independent violated contract exists; history sensitivity alone cannot certify useful personalization.

Cache bounded training examples; freeze candidates, detector rules, tolerances, and original final occupied readout. Test causality at earlier positions using equal-length inputs identical through each cut point, preserving padding. Record activation, observable change, contract outcome, alarm, and unresolved cases separately. Report fault-by-probe counts and control alarms; report detection rates only for independently adjudicated violations. Do not claim localization accuracy without known references.

Keep the existing time cap, adapter interfaces, four routes, seeds, training limits, and `finally` restoration. Calibration excludes validation and user-intent claims; host macro validation HR@10 remains authoritative.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add a bounded, independently adjudicated mutation-calibration stage before staged activation-patching diagnosis. Measure execution-path coverage and detection of specified contract violations using temporary diagnostic variants of each category’s single frozen NextItNet checkpoint; keep behavioral sensitivity and circuit localization as separate questions.",
    "motivation": "Extensive controls do not establish that the diagnostic path detects faults, and observable mutation effects do not establish degraded recommendation quality. Early calibration can expose disconnected wrappers, insensitive probes, and circular detection claims before patch effects motivate training changes. Known-path recovery is a stronger subsequent direction for localization, but requires additional infrastructure and does not replace implementation checks.",
    "implementation_notes": "Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve the actual trained view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data contracts. Use public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions only. No ratings, reviews, simulator traits, compatibility, ownership, current demand, or satisfaction may be inferred as observed facts.

Train exactly one independent NextItNet model per category as required by the host. Calibration uses that category’s resulting frozen checkpoint. Do not train, save, deploy, or combine mutated variants; they are temporary diagnostic executions sharing frozen weights. No independently fitted predictor, score fusion, or synthetic trained model is introduced. The chosen diagnostic-only modification leaves deployed architecture and inference unchanged, preserving checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency.

Cache at most two training-loader batches and select at most 16 uniquely identifiable training users per category with a local RNG seed of 42. Reject ambiguous identity matches with counts. Preserve input width and original aligned positives and negatives. For endpoint scores use the maximum occupied index, never count−1; exclude empty rows and invalid aligned candidate pairs. Use the same candidates across compared conditions, including identical candidate IDs across different-history tests. Preserve the existing staged diagnosis’s candidate construction and distinguish its target-plus-up-to-99-alternatives outcomes from loader positive/negative observations. Neither is pinned host validation.

Reserve at most 20 seconds within the existing 120-second category diagnosis budget. Check a monotonic deadline before each bounded operation, stop scheduling operations when exhausted, and record incomplete coverage and any operation overrun. GPU launches are asynchronous: use synchronized boundaries or completed CUDA timing events for measured GPU work; deadline checks cannot interrupt an already running operation. Run staged patching only with the remaining budget.

Before examining outcomes, record a replay manifest containing checkpoint identity, selected training case identifiers, candidate IDs, cut points, mutation definitions and strengths, affected modules, probe-to-fault expectations, tolerances, detector decision rules, seed, numerical configuration, and budgets. Do not tune mutation strengths, alarm thresholds, or expected mappings on these same cases. Repeated calls and perturbations within a user are dependent observations. With at most 16 users, prioritize descriptive counts; any uncertainty estimate must resample whole users and disclose its conditional, small-sample scope. Do not imply coverage of training randomness from one checkpoint.

Use scoped diagnostic callables or hooks rather than editing parameters or globally replacing public methods. Construct a separate DiagnosisProbe with the modified view so the real diagnostic entry point exercises the injected path. Keep modified_view.model identical to the trained nn.Module. Register temporary counters on the relevant modules beneath view.model, and verify the intended callable and hook execute. Invoke modules through module(...) rather than module.forward(...), which bypasses their registered forward hooks. A counter proves execution only, not correctness. Prevent recursion by retaining immutable references to original callables.

Incorrect-readout mutation: on nonempty left-padded histories where the indices differ, replace only the diagnostic readout with count−1. The independent structural oracle computes the maximum occupied index from the original sequence and compares the selected index. Record this contract violation independently of feature or score disagreement, which may be absent when features coincide. Test whether the frozen readout-agreement probe alarms through its actual execution path. Cases with identical indices are inactive for this stimulus; an active wrong index with unchanged scores is still an index-contract violation, not proven equivalence.

Future-access mutation: use intermediate sequence features, not final-position scores. For each eligible sequence, select up to three deterministic cut points from its valid interior positions: earliest, midpoint, and latest, removing duplicates. Add boundary cases adjacent to declared dilation boundaries only if they fit the cap and record the exact resulting cut points. Construct equal-length paired inputs identical through t, changing only a later occupied token and keeping every padding position unchanged. Select the earliest qualifying later position j and a deterministic different nonreserved item ID, excluding supplied candidates and observed training items; abstain if unavailable. The diagnostic variant changes only feature position t using h'_t = h_t + h_j, leaving other positions unchanged. This is a deliberately artificial diagnostic fault, not an in-distribution patch. Record hook/call activation and actual source-feature changes separately. Independently compare all output features at positions ≤t between paired inputs using torch.testing.assert_close or the equivalent explicit tolerance predicate. Check the unmodified path first; if it already violates prefix invariance, report an observed baseline contract failure and do not attribute the failure uniquely to injection. A mutation whose source or prefix difference is numerically silent is unresolved under this stimulus, not proven unreachable or equivalent. Run the frozen prefix diagnostic on the modified view and record its alarm separately from the oracle outcome.

Constant-feature mutation: broadcast a fixed zero FP32 feature vector of the correct hidden size across histories and positions. Compare distinct histories using identical candidate IDs, recording activation, resulting feature/score equality, and the existing history-sensitivity alarm. If the baseline also produces indistinguishable outputs, mark the behavioral challenge unresolved. There is no universal correctness requirement that every pair of histories yield different recommendations. Consequently this challenge is excluded from contract-detection accuracy denominators unless a separate, predeclared contract justifies a label. It does not establish shortcut learning or faulty personalization in the unmodified model.

Predeclare FP32 feature and score tolerances, initially atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5. Compare |a−b| against atol+rtol*|b| using a declared reference b; invalidate nonfinite results rather than treating them as passes. Record execution activation, observable behavioral change, independently adjudicated contract outcome, and detector alarm as separate fields. An independent reference calculation must not simply call the detector or reuse its final alarm. For intrinsically identical oracle and probe assertions, label the result an integration self-check, not independent detector validation.

For every fault-by-probe cell report scheduled, executed, active, independently violated, independently passed, unresolved, invalid, alarmed, and not-run counts, with reasons. Report detection rate only as alarms among independently established violations, with its explicit denominator. Report alarm rates on unchanged and identity-hook controls; call these false alarms only where an independent oracle establishes that the relevant tested property holds. Baseline controls may reveal genuine defects. Do not call output disagreement a killed mutant, and do not import DeepCrime’s aggregate killing claims: its repeated-training significance and minimum-effect requirements are not met here. Do not apply MuFF’s suite-sensitivity terminology to detector sensitivity. Avoid an aggregate mutation or health score; redundant easy mutants could inflate it. Descriptors such as inactive, invalid, unresolved, and behaviorally indistinguishable under tested inputs are preferable to unsupported claims of equivalence or unreachability.

Run unchanged and identity-hook controls on the same examples and candidates. Keep deterministic evaluation, gradients disabled, and FP32 execution. Save and restore per-module training modes, RNG states, backend settings if modified, and hooks in finally, including on deadline or exceptions. Control failures invalidate affected comparisons, not unrelated results automatically. Retain existing controls for batch consistency, repeatability, padding/layout, identity patches, and readout agreement.

Do not infer component-localization accuracy from injected fault placement or detection. A known injection site identifies the imposed defect, not the natural mechanism supporting recommendations. Return localization accuracy as null with a reason unless independently specified ground-truth paths exist. Later known-path calibration should use exact synthetic references, matched-size random and irrelevant-site controls, and separate restoration/disruption tests; precision/recall requires a defined reference edge or component universe. Such work is a separate proposal, with no extra trained predictor in this experiment. Natural-model activation patches remain corruption- and metric-dependent, and hybrid-state distances cannot certify intervention validity. Joint patches may expose interactions but increase cost and require prespecified scope.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. All calibration consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not inspect other trials, hidden tests, or extra data, and do not reconstruct unavailable pinned validation candidates. Export parity remains explicitly unverified until independently checked. Host macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection criterion. No implementation or new results are claimed here.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = capture_per_module_execution_state(self.view.model)
        handles = []
        metrics, definitions = {}, calibration_definitions()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with deterministic_fp32_no_grad():
                cached = bounded_training_cache(train_loader, max_batches=2)
                cases = select_identifiable_cases(cached, max_users=16, seed=42)
                # Correct endpoint index is max occupied index, never count-1.
                reference = evaluate_correct_adapter(cases)
                protocol = freeze_protocol_before_observing_outcomes(cases)
                save_trial_local_replay_manifest(protocol)
                controls = independently_adjudicate_and_run_controls(cases, reference)
                metrics['controls'] = controls

                for fault in ['wrong_readout', 'future_feature_mix', 'constant_features']:
                    if calibration_deadline_reached():
                        record_not_run(metrics, fault, 'Calibration budget exhausted')
                        continue
                    if relevant_control_invalid(controls, fault):
                        record_invalid(metrics, fault, controls)
                        continue
                    # Same frozen nn.Module; scoped callables/hooks, no fitted model.
                    with scoped_diagnostic_variant(self.view, fault, protocol) as variant:
                        probe = DiagnosisProbe(variant.view, self.device)
                        witness = independently_record_activation_and_behavior(
                            variant, cases, protocol)
                        oracle = adjudicate_declared_contract(
                            fault, witness, cases, reference, protocol)
                        # Constant features normally have no correctness label.
                        # Equivalent oracle/probe assertions count only as self-checks.
                        alarms = probe.run_frozen_target_probes(
                            cases, protocol, calibration_enabled=False)
                        record_separate_fields(metrics, fault, witness, oracle, alarms)

                summarize_fault_probe_counts_with_explicit_denominators(metrics)
                report_control_alarm_rates_with_oracle_status(metrics, controls)
                metrics['localization_accuracy'] = {
                    'value': None,
                    'missing_reason': 'No independently specified reference circuit.'}
                run_valid_staged_patching_with_remaining_budget(metrics, controls)
        finally:
            remove_scoped_hooks_even_on_failure(handles)
            restore_per_module_execution_state(self.view.model, state)
        return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

# Internal calibration must not recursively call run_full_diagnosis.
# Future contract oracle: paired equal-length sequences agree through t;
# preserve padding; compare every feature position <= t, not just final scores.
# All repeats remain clustered by original user; no pooled independent-draw claims.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_evidence_linked_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        distinguish_execution_behavior_oracle_and_alarm=True,
        require_explicit_denominators_and_unresolved_cases=True,
        forbid_unverified_localization_validation_or_user_intent_claims=True)
",
